references.text: Basic instructions regarding the grain offering (mincha), which form the background for the special grain offering in the jealousy test.
Prohibition against using leaven in the grain offering, relating to the specific requirements for the offering in the jealousy test.
Another case where a grain offering is brought without oil or frankincense, namely the sin offering for a poor person. Barley flour is also used here.
Description of mincha as a memorial portion (azkarah), corresponding to the expression 'minchat zikkaron' in the jealousy test.
Continuation of the ritual where the grain offering is called 'minchat haqena'ot' (the jealousy offering), elaborating on the purpose of the offering.
The priest takes the offering from the woman's hand, waves it, and burns the memorial portion on the altar, completing the sacrificial ritual described in verse 15.
The term 'azkarah' (memorial portion) is used here for the grain offering, relating to 'minchat zikkaron' (memorial offering) in the jealousy test.
Hosea describes Israel's unfaithfulness to God using imagery of jealousy, where barley is mentioned in connection with unfaithfulness.
